# Recipes

A recipe is a verified [`http`](plan-format.md#the-generic-http-adapter) spec for one operation of one provider,
shipped with Sponson: the line names it and fills in its params, and the requests, envelopes, ids and drift rules
come from the recipe. Everything the generic adapter guarantees holds unchanged (intents before creates, idempotent
apply, drift by hash, destroy only what Sponson created). Why and how: [ADR 0020](adr/0020-recipes.md).

```yaml
providers:
  http:
    cloudflare: { recipe: cloudflare }   # optional: the recipe's API defaults; override base_url, auth, headers here
changes:
  - id: preview_dns
    adapter: http
    op: resource                         # the recipe's kind: resource or list_item
    recipe: cloudflare.dns_cname
    zone_id: 023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353
    name: "${ctx.scope}.preview.example.com"
    target: preview-host.example.net
```

- `recipe: <provider>.<op>` picks the operation; `api` defaults to `<provider>`, and so does its block under
  `providers.http`: write the block only to override `base_url`, `base_url_env`, `auth`, `headers` or `encoding`.
- Every other key of the line is one of the recipe's params. Values are literals, `${ctx.*}`, `{ from }`,
  `{ secret }` or `{ keep: true }`, as anywhere in a plan. An unknown param, a missing required one or a value of
  the wrong type is `PARAM_INVALID` naming it, before any request; an unknown recipe or op lists the known ones.
- `destroy: keep` leaves what the line made in place when the scope is destroyed.
- Identity: the ledger records the API block as resolved (base URL, credential variable, headers, encoding) and the
  keys and record ids of the expanded requests, never the recipe's text. A line written by hand with the same
  values is the same resource, and a new Sponson version whose recipe changes only its docs, params or assumptions
  re-identifies nothing.

Every op below is tested by `scenarios/recipes.test.ts` against the local fake cloud (create, idempotent re-apply,
drift, destroy), and live with `pnpm test:live` when its credential and the `SPONSON_LIVE_*` variables its recipe
names are set.

| Recipe | Op | What it manages | Credential |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`cloudflare.dns_cname`](#cloudflaredns_cname) | `resource` | DNS CNAME record | `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` (bearer) |
| [`configcat.targeting_rule`](#configcattargeting_rule) | `list_item` | Feature flag targeting rule | `CONFIGCAT_BASIC_AUTH_USERNAME` / `CONFIGCAT_BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD` (basic) |

## Cloudflare

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/cloudflare.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/cloudflare.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Create DNS record](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/create/)
- [List DNS records](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/list/)
- [DNS record details](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/get/)
- [Update DNS record (PATCH)](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/edit/)
- [Delete DNS record](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/delete/)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4` |
| `base_url_env` | `CLOUDFLARE_API_URL` |
| Credential | `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` (bearer) |

Assumptions:

- **CF1** (verified, [source](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/create/)): Records are created with `POST /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records` (`type`, `name`, `content`, `ttl`, `proxied`, `comment`), authenticated with an API token as `Authorization: Bearer` that has DNS Write on the zone.
- **CF2** (verified, [source](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/list/)): `GET /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records` answers `{ result: [...] }` and filters by `type` and `name.exact` (names compare case-insensitively).
- **CF3** (verified, [source](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/get/)): Single-record answers (create, details, update) carry the record under `result`, with its `id`.
- **CF4** (verified, [source](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/delete/)): `PATCH /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records/{id}` updates a record; `DELETE` on the same path removes it permanently.
- **CF5** **(unverified)**: A PATCH needs `name` and `type` alongside the changed fields (the edit schema does not mark them optional), so every update sends both.
- **CF6** **(unverified)**: The API returns `name` lower-cased as the full name and `content` as written, so `name` must be given lower-case and fully qualified, or every plan finds no record and tries to create one.
- **CF7** **(unverified)**: A proxied record reports `ttl: 1` (automatic) whatever was sent, so `ttl` other than 1 with `proxied: true` shows as drift on every plan.
- **CF8** (verified, [source](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/create/)): A CNAME cannot share its name with another record, so name and type identify it within the zone and a filtered list holds at most one, on its first page.

### `cloudflare.dns_cname`

**DNS CNAME record** (`http.resource`). A CNAME record in a zone, such as `pr-42.preview.example.com` pointing at the preview deployment's host. Located by name and type; a console edit of its target, proxying, TTL or comment is drift.

Covers: `cloudflare-dns` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`, `hostname`. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `zone_id` | string | yes | — | The zone's id (32 hex characters, on the zone's Overview page). Matches `^[0-9a-f]{32}$`. |
| `name` | string | yes | — | The record's full name, lower-case, zone included. Matches `^[a-z0-9*_.-]+$`. |
| `target` | string | yes | — | The host the name points at (the record's `content`). |
| `proxied` | boolean | no | `false` | Whether Cloudflare proxies the traffic. |
| `ttl` | integer | no | `1` | TTL in seconds (60–86400), or 1 for automatic. |
| `comment` | string | no | — | A note on the record; no effect on DNS. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: dns_cname
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: cloudflare.dns_cname
  zone_id: 023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353
  name: ${ctx.scope}.preview.example.com
  target: preview-host.example.net
  comment: Managed by Sponson
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
find:
  path: /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records?type=CNAME&name.exact={name}
  list_path: /result
  match:
    type: CNAME
    name: { param: name }
create:
  path: /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records
update:
  method: PATCH
  path: /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records/{id}
  body:
    type: CNAME
    name: { param: name }
delete:
  path: /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records/{id}
item_path: /result
fields:
  content: { param: target }
  proxied: { param: proxied }
  ttl: { param: ttl }
  comment: { param: comment }
outputs:
  hostname: /name
```

## ConfigCat

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/configcat.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/configcat.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Public Management API](https://api.configcat.com/docs/)
- [OpenAPI spec (get value v2, replace value v2, targeting rule models)](https://api.configcat.com/docs/v1/swagger.json)
- [Terraform provider (credential variable names)](https://github.com/configcat/terraform-provider-configcat/blob/main/docs/index.md)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://api.configcat.com` |
| `base_url_env` | `CONFIGCAT_API_URL` |
| Credential | `CONFIGCAT_BASIC_AUTH_USERNAME` / `CONFIGCAT_BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD` (basic) |

Assumptions:

- **CC1** (verified, [source](https://api.configcat.com/docs/v1/swagger.json)): The API is at `https://api.configcat.com`, authenticated with Basic auth from Public API credentials (the Terraform provider's `CONFIGCAT_BASIC_AUTH_USERNAME` / `CONFIGCAT_BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD`).
- **CC2** (verified, [source](https://api.configcat.com/docs/v1/swagger.json)): `GET /v2/environments/{environmentId}/settings/{settingId}/value` answers the setting's value in the environment bare: `defaultValue`, `targetingRules`, `percentageEvaluationAttribute` and read-only fields.
- **CC3** (verified, [source](https://api.configcat.com/docs/v1/swagger.json)): `PUT` on the same path replaces the value: only `defaultValue`, `targetingRules` and `percentageEvaluationAttribute` can be set, and one not sent is reset. So those three are sent, as read, with the rule list changed (`parent.send`).
- **CC4** (verified, [source](https://api.configcat.com/docs/v1/swagger.json)): A targeting rule is `{ conditions: [{ userCondition: { comparisonAttribute, comparator, comparisonValue: { stringValue, doubleValue, listValue: [{ value, hint }] } } }], value | percentageOptions }`; rules have no id and are evaluated in order. `isOneOf` and `sensitiveIsOneOf` compare a user attribute with a list.
- **CC5** (verified, [source](https://api.configcat.com/docs/v1/swagger.json)): Answers carry every member of a value (`boolValue`, `stringValue`, `intValue`, `doubleValue`, `predefinedVariationId`) and of a comparison value, the unused ones null; the rule is written with the same nulls so that it reads back equal.
- **CC6** **(unverified)**: A condition is read back with `segmentCondition` and `prerequisiteFlagCondition` null and each list value's `hint` null, exactly as written; otherwise every plan shows the rule as changed.
- **CC7** **(unverified)**: In a product with "Config changes require a reason" or approvals turned on, the PUT without `reason` / `bypassApproval` is refused (the query parameters are not sent); the apply then fails.

### `configcat.targeting_rule`

**Feature flag targeting rule** (`http.list_item`). A targeting rule on a boolean feature flag in one environment that serves a value to the preview, such as `IF Preview IS ONE OF [pr-42] THEN true`. Added after the flag's other rules (evaluated in order: an earlier matching rule wins); the default value and the other rules are written back as read. Identified by the matched value; a console edit of its condition or served value is drift. Destroy removes the rule.

Covers: `configcat-rule` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: none. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `environment_id` | string | yes | — | The environment's id (a UUID). |
| `setting_id` | string | yes | — | The feature flag's numeric setting id. Matches `^[0-9]+$`. |
| `attribute` | string | yes | — | The user attribute the rule compares (a custom attribute such as `Preview`, or `Identifier`, `Email`). |
| `comparator` | string | no | `isOneOf` | `isOneOf`, or `sensitiveIsOneOf` (hashed in the config JSON). One of `isOneOf`, `sensitiveIsOneOf`. |
| `match` | string | yes | — | The attribute value that is the preview; it identifies the rule. |
| `serve` | boolean | no | `true` | The value the flag serves to the preview. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: targeting_rule
  adapter: http
  op: list_item
  recipe: configcat.targeting_rule
  environment_id: 08d8becf-d4d9-4c66-8b48-6ac74cd95fba
  setting_id: "12345"
  attribute: Preview
  match: ${ctx.scope}
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.list_item`](plan-format.md#httplist_item) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
parent:
  path: /v2/environments/{environment_id}/settings/{setting_id}/value
  method: PUT
  send:
    - defaultValue
    - percentageEvaluationAttribute
list_path: /targetingRules
key_field: /conditions/0/userCondition/comparisonValue/listValue/0/value
item:
  conditions:
    - userCondition:
        comparisonAttribute: { param: attribute }
        comparator: { param: comparator }
        comparisonValue:
          stringValue: null
          doubleValue: null
          listValue:
            - value: { param: match }
              hint: null
      segmentCondition: null
      prerequisiteFlagCondition: null
  value:
    boolValue: { param: serve }
    stringValue: null
    intValue: null
    doubleValue: null
    predefinedVariationId: null
```

## GitHub

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/github.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/github.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [REST API endpoints for repository webhooks](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/webhooks)
- [Authenticating to the REST API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/authentication/authenticating-to-the-rest-api)
- [Getting started with the REST API (headers, API versions)](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://api.github.com` |
| `base_url_env` | `GITHUB_API_URL` |
| Credential | `GITHUB_TOKEN` (bearer) |
| `headers` | {"X-GitHub-Api-Version":"2022-11-28","User-Agent":"sponson"} |

Assumptions:

- **GH1** (verified, [source](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/webhooks)): `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks` creates a repository webhook from `name: web`, `config` (`url`, `content_type`, `secret`, `insecure_ssl`), `events` and `active`, answering 201 with the hook (its integer `id` and `config`), authenticated with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- **GH2** (verified, [source](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/webhooks)): `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks` answers a bare array of hooks, each with `config.url`; it pages with `per_page` (at most 100) and `page`.
- **GH3** (verified, [source](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/webhooks)): `PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks/{hook_id}` updates `config`, `events` (replacing the list) and `active`; a secret set before is removed unless the same or a new one is sent, so every update sends the config's `url` and `secret` again.
- **GH4** (verified, [source](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/webhooks)): `DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks/{hook_id}` answers 204, and 404 when the hook is gone.
- **GH5** (verified, [source](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/webhooks)): Each hook should have a unique config, and hooks may share one only when their events do not overlap. The recipe takes the URL as the hook's identity; two hooks with the same URL make `find` refuse (PARAM_INVALID) instead of guessing.
- **GH6** **(unverified)**: The secret is write-only: answers carry it masked or not at all, so it is sent on create and update but never compared, and a secret changed in the plan reaches GitHub only with the next change of a compared field. Keep it in a secret manager and reference it with `{ secret: … }`.
- **GH7** **(unverified)**: A repository has at most 100 hooks for this purpose (GitHub limits hooks per event), so the first page of `?per_page=100` holds the one `find` looks for.
- **GH8** **(unverified)**: `config.content_type` and `config.insecure_ssl` are answered as sent (`json`/`form`, the strings `"0"`/`"1"`), and `Accept: application/json` is served like `application/vnd.github+json`.
- **GH9** **(unverified)**: The token needs the repository permission Webhooks (write) or the classic `admin:repo_hook` scope; the `GITHUB_TOKEN` of GitHub Actions does not have it, so use a GitHub App token or a fine-grained token. `GITHUB_API_URL` (set by Actions) points at GitHub Enterprise Server where that is the host.

### `github.repo_webhook`

**Repository webhook** (`http.resource`). A repository webhook delivering to an environment's URL, such as the preview deployment's `/api/github` handler. Located by its URL; a console edit of its events, its active flag, its content type or its TLS check is drift. The secret is sent but not compared (GH6).

Covers: `github-webhook` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `owner` | string | yes | — | The repository's owner (user or organization). |
| `repo` | string | yes | — | The repository's name. |
| `url` | string | yes | — | The URL GitHub delivers to; it identifies the hook in the repository. Matches `^https?://\\S+$`. |
| `events` | list | no | `["push"]` | The events that trigger a delivery (`["*"]` for all). |
| `active` | boolean | no | `true` | Whether deliveries are sent. |
| `content_type` | string | no | `json` | The payload's media type. One of `json`, `form`. |
| `insecure_ssl` | string | no | `0` | "1" skips verifying the TLS certificate of the URL. One of `0`, `1`. |
| `secret` | string | no | — | The secret deliveries are signed with (write-only; GH6). Use `{ secret: … }`. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: repo_webhook
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: github.repo_webhook
  owner: acme
  repo: app
  url: https://${ctx.scope}.preview.example.com/api/github
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
find:
  path: /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks?per_page=100
  match:
    /config/url: { param: url }
create:
  path: /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks
  body:
    name: web
    config:
      secret: { param: secret }
update:
  method: PATCH
  path: /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks/{id}
  body:
    config:
      url: { param: url }
      secret: { param: secret }
delete:
  path: /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks/{id}
fields:
  active: { param: active }
  events: { param: events }
  /config/content_type: { param: content_type }
  /config/insecure_ssl: { param: insecure_ssl }
```

## GrowthBook

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/growthbook.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/growthbook.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [REST API reference (authentication, versioning)](https://docs.growthbook.io/api)
- [Get a feature (v2)](https://docs.growthbook.io/api#operation/getFeatureV2)
- [Update a feature (v2)](https://docs.growthbook.io/api#operation/updateFeatureV2)
- [OpenAPI spec](https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/openapi.yaml)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://api.growthbook.io/api` |
| `base_url_env` | `GROWTHBOOK_API_URL` |
| Credential | `GROWTHBOOK_API_KEY` (bearer) |

Assumptions:

- **GB1** (verified, [source](https://docs.growthbook.io/api)): GrowthBook Cloud's API is at `https://api.growthbook.io/api` (self-hosted: its API host plus `/api`), authenticated with a secret key or personal access token as `Authorization: Bearer`.
- **GB2** (verified, [source](https://docs.growthbook.io/api#operation/getFeatureV2)): The v1 feature endpoints (rules per environment) are deprecated; in v2 a feature's rules are one top-level `rules` array, each rule naming its `environments` (or `allEnvironments`).
- **GB3** (verified, [source](https://docs.growthbook.io/api#operation/getFeatureV2)): `GET /v2/features/{id}` answers `{ feature: { …, rules: [...] } }`.
- **GB4** (verified, [source](https://docs.growthbook.io/api#operation/updateFeatureV2)): `POST /v2/features/{id}` patch-merges the top-level fields it is sent, and `rules`, when sent, replaces the whole array: so the array is read, the rule added or changed, and the whole array sent back. Rules read with GET may be posted back unchanged. The update publishes a new revision at once.
- **GB5** (verified, [source](https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/openapi.yaml)): A force rule is `{ type: force, description, condition, value, enabled, allEnvironments, environments }`; `condition` is a JSON query serialised as a string and `value` is a string (`"true"` for a boolean feature).
- **GB6** **(unverified)**: Rule ids may be chosen by the client but what the server does with them is not documented, so the rule is identified by its `description`, which it stores as written; two rules with that description are one rule to Sponson.
- **GB7** **(unverified)**: A rule is read back with `condition` exactly as sent (not reformatted), so the compared fields do not show as changed on every plan.
- **GB8** (verified, [source](https://docs.growthbook.io/api#operation/updateFeatureV2)): When the feature requires approval, the update answers 422 with the gates that blocked it, unless the organisation lets the REST API bypass approvals; the apply then fails.

### `growthbook.force_rule`

**Feature force rule** (`http.list_item`). A force rule on an existing feature that serves a value to the preview in one environment, such as `value "true"` when `{"preview": "pr-42"}`. Added after the feature's other rules (rules are evaluated in order: an earlier rule that matches the preview wins). A console edit of its condition, value, environments or enabled state is drift. Destroy removes the rule.

Covers: `growthbook-force-rule` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: none. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `feature_id` | string | yes | — | The feature's key. |
| `environment` | string | yes | — | The environment the rule applies in. |
| `description` | string | yes | — | The rule's description, unique among the feature's rules; it identifies the rule. |
| `condition` | string | yes | — | The targeting condition, a JSON query as a string. |
| `value` | string | yes | — | The value served, as a string (`"true"` for a boolean feature, JSON for a JSON feature). |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | `true` | Whether the rule is on. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: force_rule
  adapter: http
  op: list_item
  recipe: growthbook.force_rule
  feature_id: new-checkout
  environment: staging
  description: Sponson preview ${ctx.scope}
  condition: '{"preview": "${ctx.scope}"}'
  value: "true"
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.list_item`](plan-format.md#httplist_item) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
parent:
  path: /v2/features/{feature_id}
  method: POST
  item_path: /feature
list_path: /rules
key_field: description
item:
  description: { param: description }
  type: force
  condition: { param: condition }
  value: { param: value }
  enabled: { param: enabled }
  allEnvironments: false
  environments:
    - { param: environment }
```

- [Create a Marker](https://docs.honeycomb.io/api/markers/create-a-marker)
- [List All Markers](https://docs.honeycomb.io/api/markers)
- [Update a Marker](https://docs.honeycomb.io/api/markers/update-a-marker)
- [Delete a Marker](https://docs.honeycomb.io/api/markers/delete-a-marker)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://api.honeycomb.io` |
| `base_url_env` | `HONEYCOMB_API_URL` |
| Credential | `HONEYCOMB_API_KEY` (header `X-Honeycomb-Team`) |

Assumptions:

- **HC1** (verified, [source](https://docs.honeycomb.io/api/markers/create-a-marker)): `POST /1/markers/{datasetSlug}` creates a marker from `start_time`, `end_time` (Unix seconds), `message`, `type` and `url` (all optional; `start_time` defaults to the request's arrival), answering 201 with the marker and its `id`; `__all__` as the dataset slug makes an environment-wide marker. Requests carry a Configuration Key with the Manage Markers permission in `X-Honeycomb-Team`.
- **HC2** (verified, [source](https://docs.honeycomb.io/api/markers)): `GET /1/markers/{datasetSlug}` answers a bare array of the dataset's markers (`id`, `message`, `type`, `url`, `start_time`, `end_time`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `color`).
- **HC3** (verified, [source](https://docs.honeycomb.io/api/markers/update-a-marker)): `PUT /1/markers/{datasetSlug}/{markerId}` replaces the marker: a field left out of the body is erased.
- **HC4** (verified, [source](https://docs.honeycomb.io/api/markers/delete-a-marker)): `DELETE /1/markers/{datasetSlug}/{markerId}` removes the marker and answers it (200).
- **HC5** (verified, [source](https://docs.honeycomb.io/api/markers/create-a-marker)): The API is served from `api.honeycomb.io` (US) and `api.eu1.honeycomb.io` (EU); EU teams set `base_url` in the provider block.
- **HC6** **(unverified)**: Message and type identify the marker this recipe created among the dataset's markers (Honeycomb does not require them to be unique: two equal ones make `find` refuse with PARAM_INVALID), and the list holds every marker of the dataset in one answer.
- **HC7** **(unverified)**: An update (a changed `url`) re-sends message, type and url but not `start_time`, which Honeycomb then sets to the time of the update (HC3), moving the marker; markers are rarely edited.
- **HC8** **(unverified)**: A deleted marker answers 404 to DELETE, which destroy treats as already gone.

### `honeycomb.marker`

**Deploy marker** (`http.resource`). A marker on an environment's dataset (or on every dataset of the environment with `__all__`) for a deploy, such as `deploy pr-42 0123abc`. Located by its message and type; a console edit of its URL is drift. Destroying the scope removes it; write `destroy: keep` to keep the deploy history.

Covers: `honeycomb-marker` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dataset` | string | yes | — | The dataset's slug, or `__all__` for an environment-wide marker. |
| `message` | string | yes | — | The marker's text; with its type, its identity (HC6). |
| `type` | string | no | `deploy` | The marker's type, which groups markers (and their color). |
| `url` | string | no | — | The link opened from the marker (the preview or the build). |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: marker
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: honeycomb.marker
  dataset: __all__
  message: deploy ${ctx.scope} ${ctx.git.sha}
  url: https://${ctx.scope}.preview.example.com
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
find:
  path: /1/markers/{dataset}
  match:
    message: { param: message }
    type: { param: type }
create:
  path: /1/markers/{dataset}
update:
  method: PUT
  path: /1/markers/{dataset}/{id}
delete:
  path: /1/markers/{dataset}/{id}
fields:
  url: { param: url }
```

## PostHog

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/posthog.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/posthog.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Private API (hosts, personal API keys)](https://posthog.com/docs/api)
- [Feature flags API](https://posthog.com/docs/api/feature-flags)
- [OpenAPI schema (FeatureFlag, PersonalAPIKeyAuth)](https://us.posthog.com/api/schema/?format=json)
- [Feature flag serializer (filters validation and merge)](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/products/feature_flags/backend/api/feature_flag.py)
- [Feature flag filters schema (condition groups)](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/products/feature_flags/backend/api/filters_schema.py)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://us.posthog.com` |
| `base_url_env` | `POSTHOG_API_URL` |
| Credential | `POSTHOG_PERSONAL_API_KEY` (bearer) |

Assumptions:

- **PH1** (verified, [source](https://posthog.com/docs/api)): The private API is at `https://us.posthog.com` (US cloud) or `https://eu.posthog.com` (EU cloud; set `base_url`), authenticated with a personal API key as `Authorization: Bearer`, with the `feature_flag:read` and `feature_flag:write` scopes.
- **PH2** (verified, [source](https://us.posthog.com/api/schema/?format=json)): `GET /api/projects/{project_id}/feature_flags/{id}/` (trailing slash) answers the flag bare, with its release conditions in `filters.groups`; `PATCH` on the same path updates it and answers it bare.
- **PH3** (verified, [source](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/products/feature_flags/backend/api/filters_schema.py)): A condition group is `{ properties: [{ key, type, operator, value }], rollout_percentage, variant }`; `exact` takes a list of values. Groups have no id, so the group is identified by the first value of its first property (the preview host).
- **PH4** (verified, [source](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/products/feature_flags/backend/api/feature_flag.py)): A PATCH of `filters` merges top-level keys into the stored filters (`{**stored_filters, **filters}`): sending `{ filters: { groups } }` replaces the groups and keeps `multivariate`, `payloads` and the rest. This is in the serializer's source, not the docs.
- **PH5** **(unverified)**: Self-hosted or older PostHog versions merge `filters` the same way (the merge arrived with 2026's validation work). On a version that replaces `filters` whole, every write would drop the flag's variants and payloads: check before pointing the recipe at one.
- **PH6** **(unverified)**: A group is read back as written (the serializer drops unknown keys and adds none to the declared ones), so the compared `properties`, `rollout_percentage` and `variant` do not show as changed on every plan.
- **PH7** (verified, [source](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/products/approvals/backend/decorators.py)): A flag under an approval policy answers a PATCH with 409 (`approval_required` or `change_request_pending`); the apply then fails with PROVIDER_CONFLICT rather than waiting for the approval.

### `posthog.release_condition`

**Flag release condition** (`http.list_item`). A release condition (condition group) on an existing feature flag that matches the preview, such as `$host exact [pr-42.preview.example.com]` at 100%. Groups are OR'd; the flag's other groups, variants and payloads are left as they are. A console edit of its properties, rollout or variant is drift. Destroy removes the group (with the last group gone, the flag matches no one).

Covers: `posthog-release-condition` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: none. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project_id` | string | yes | — | The project's numeric id (Project settings). Matches `^[0-9]+$`. |
| `flag_id` | string | yes | — | The flag's numeric id (in the flag's URL), not its key. Matches `^[0-9]+$`. |
| `property` | string | yes | — | The property the condition tests. It must be known when the flag is evaluated (a person property, or one passed with the evaluation). |
| `property_type` | string | no | `person` | Whether `property` is a person or a group property. One of `person`, `group`. |
| `operator` | string | no | `exact` | How the property is compared with `value`. One of `exact`, `is_not`, `icontains`, `regex`. |
| `value` | string | yes | — | The value that matches the preview (such as its host); it identifies the condition on the flag. |
| `rollout_percentage` | integer | no | `100` | The share of matching users the flag is on for (0–100). |
| `variant` | string | no | — | For a multivariate flag, the variant the condition serves. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: release_condition
  adapter: http
  op: list_item
  recipe: posthog.release_condition
  project_id: "12345"
  flag_id: "678"
  property: $host
  value: ${ctx.scope}.preview.example.com
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.list_item`](plan-format.md#httplist_item) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
parent:
  path: /api/projects/{project_id}/feature_flags/{flag_id}/
  method: PATCH
list_path: /filters/groups
key_field: /properties/0/value/0
item:
  properties:
    - key: { param: property }
      type: { param: property_type }
      operator: { param: operator }
      value:
        - { param: value }
  rollout_percentage: { param: rollout_percentage }
  variant: { param: variant }
```

## Postmark (Account API)

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/postmark.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/postmark.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Servers API](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/api/servers-api)
- [API overview (authentication)](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/api/overview)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://api.postmarkapp.com` |
| `base_url_env` | `POSTMARK_API_URL` |
| Credential | `POSTMARK_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` (header `X-Postmark-Account-Token`) |

Assumptions:

- **PM1** (verified, [source](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/api/servers-api)): The Servers API authenticates with the account token in `X-Postmark-Account-Token` (account owner only) and takes and answers JSON.
- **PM2** (verified, [source](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/api/servers-api)): `POST /servers` creates a server from `Name` (required), `Color`, `DeliveryType` (`Live` or `Sandbox`, fixed after creation), `InboundHookUrl`, `TrackOpens`, `TrackLinks` and more, answering the server with its integer `ID`, its settings and `ApiTokens` (the server's tokens).
- **PM3** (verified, [source](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/api/servers-api)): `GET /servers?count=&offset=&name=` answers `{ TotalCount, Servers: [...] }`; `name` is a substring search (`MyServer` also matches `MyServer Production`), so the recipe matches the exact `Name` among the results.
- **PM4** (verified, [source](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/api/servers-api)): `PUT /servers/{serverid}` changes the settings sent (everything but `DeliveryType`); `GET /servers/{serverid}` answers the server with its `ApiTokens`, so the server token stays readable.
- **PM5** (verified, [source](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/api/servers-api)): `DELETE /servers/{serverid}` removes a server, but is not enabled for every account: where Postmark support has not enabled it, destroy fails and the line needs `destroy: keep`.
- **PM6** **(unverified)**: Server names are unique in the account (a second create with the same name is refused), and an account has fewer than 500 servers, so the first page of `count=500` holds the one `find` looks for.
- **PM7** **(unverified)**: `Color`, `TrackOpens`, `TrackLinks` and `InboundHookUrl` are answered as sent (`InboundHookUrl` empty when unset), so they compare without drift.

### `postmark.server`

**Server** (`http.resource`). A Postmark server per environment, such as `sponson-preview-pr-42`, with its inbound webhook URL and tracking settings. Its token is a sensitive output for the app's environment (`{ from: <line>.server_token }`). Located by its name; a console edit of its color, tracking or inbound hook URL is drift. Webhooks of the server's message streams need the server's own token: see `postmark_server.webhook`.

Covers: — in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`, `server_token` (sensitive). On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | The server's name, unique in the account (PM6); its identity. |
| `color` | string | no | `Blue` | The server's color in the Postmark dashboard. One of `Purple`, `Blue`, `Turquoise`, `Green`, `Red`, `Yellow`, `Grey`, `Orange`. |
| `delivery_type` | string | no | `Sandbox` | `Sandbox` accepts mail without delivering it; fixed once the server exists (sent on create only). One of `Live`, `Sandbox`. |
| `inbound_hook_url` | string | no | `` | The URL inbound mail is posted to (empty for none). |
| `track_opens` | boolean | no | `false` | Track opens of outbound mail. |
| `track_links` | string | no | `None` | Track link clicks of outbound mail. One of `None`, `HtmlAndText`, `HtmlOnly`, `TextOnly`. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: server
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: postmark.server
  name: sponson-${ctx.env}-${ctx.scope}
  inbound_hook_url: https://${ctx.scope}.preview.example.com/api/postmark/inbound
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
find:
  path: /servers?count=500&offset=0&name={name}
  list_path: /Servers
  match:
    Name: { param: name }
create:
  path: /servers
  body:
    DeliveryType: { param: delivery_type }
update:
  method: PUT
  path: /servers/{id}
delete:
  path: /servers/{id}
id_path: /ID
fields:
  Color: { param: color }
  InboundHookUrl: { param: inbound_hook_url }
  TrackOpens: { param: track_opens }
  TrackLinks: { param: track_links }
outputs:
  server_token:
    path: /ApiTokens/0
    sensitive: true
```

## Postmark (Server API)

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/postmark_server.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/postmark_server.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Webhooks API](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/api/webhooks-api)
- [API overview (authentication)](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/api/overview)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://api.postmarkapp.com` |
| `base_url_env` | `POSTMARK_API_URL` |
| Credential | `POSTMARK_SERVER_TOKEN` (header `X-Postmark-Server-Token`) |

Assumptions:

- **PS1** (verified, [source](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/api/webhooks-api)): The Webhooks API authenticates with a server's token in `X-Postmark-Server-Token`, so it manages the webhooks of that one server.
- **PS2** (verified, [source](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/api/webhooks-api)): `POST /webhooks` creates a webhook from `Url` (required), `MessageStream` (default `outbound`), `HttpAuth`, `HttpHeaders` and `Triggers` (`Open { Enabled, PostFirstOpenOnly }`, `Click`, `Delivery`, `Bounce { Enabled, IncludeContent }`, `SpamComplaint { Enabled, IncludeContent }`, `SubscriptionChange`, each with `Enabled`), answering the webhook with its integer `ID`.
- **PS3** (verified, [source](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/api/webhooks-api)): `GET /webhooks` (optionally `?MessageStream=`) answers `{ Webhooks: [...] }` with each webhook's `ID`, `Url`, `MessageStream` and `Triggers`.
- **PS4** (verified, [source](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/api/webhooks-api)): `PUT /webhooks/{Id}` changes `Url`, `HttpAuth`, `HttpHeaders` and `Triggers` (not `MessageStream`), re-verifying the endpoint when the URL or the triggers change; `DELETE /webhooks/{Id}` removes it.
- **PS5** (verified, [source](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/api/webhooks-api)): Postmark tests the endpoint when a webhook is created; `Verify: false` saves it without the test (a preview that is not deployed yet would fail it).
- **PS6** **(unverified)**: A URL identifies one webhook of the server (two webhooks with the same URL, on different streams, make `find` refuse with PARAM_INVALID), and every trigger's `Enabled` is answered as a boolean even when it was not sent.
- **PS7** **(unverified)**: `PostFirstOpenOnly` and `IncludeContent` are left at Postmark's defaults; only which events are delivered is compared.

### `postmark_server.webhook`

**Webhook of a server** (`http.resource`). A webhook of one Postmark server delivering to an environment's URL, such as the preview's `/api/postmark` handler, with the events it enables. Located by its URL; a console edit of an event's `Enabled` is drift. It works with a server whose token is in `POSTMARK_SERVER_TOKEN` (a shared staging server, say): a server the same plan creates per environment has its token only as an output, which cannot be a credential.

Covers: — in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | string | yes | — | The URL events are posted to; its identity (PS6). Matches `^https?://\\S+$`. |
| `message_stream` | string | no | `outbound` | The message stream whose events are delivered (sent on create only). |
| `verify` | boolean | no | `false` | Have Postmark test the URL when the webhook is created (PS5). |
| `delivery` | boolean | no | `true` | Deliver `Delivery` events. |
| `bounce` | boolean | no | `true` | Deliver `Bounce` events. |
| `spam_complaint` | boolean | no | `true` | Deliver `SpamComplaint` events. |
| `open` | boolean | no | `false` | Deliver `Open` events. |
| `click` | boolean | no | `false` | Deliver `Click` events. |
| `subscription_change` | boolean | no | `false` | Deliver `SubscriptionChange` events. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: webhook
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: postmark_server.webhook
  url: https://${ctx.scope}.preview.example.com/api/postmark
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
find:
  path: /webhooks
  list_path: /Webhooks
  match:
    Url: { param: url }
create:
  path: /webhooks
  body:
    MessageStream: { param: message_stream }
    Verify: { param: verify }
update:
  method: PUT
  path: /webhooks/{id}
delete:
  path: /webhooks/{id}
id_path: /ID
fields:
  /Triggers/Delivery/Enabled: { param: delivery }
  /Triggers/Bounce/Enabled: { param: bounce }
  /Triggers/SpamComplaint/Enabled: { param: spam_complaint }
  /Triggers/Open/Enabled: { param: open }
  /Triggers/Click/Enabled: { param: click }
  /Triggers/SubscriptionChange/Enabled: { param: subscription_change }
```

## Resend

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/resend.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/resend.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Create API key](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/api-keys/create-api-key)
- [List API keys](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/api-keys/list-api-keys)
- [Delete API key](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/api-keys/delete-api-key)
- [Create webhook](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/webhooks/create-webhook)
- [Retrieve webhook](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/webhooks/get-webhook)
- [List webhooks](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/webhooks/list-webhooks)
- [Update webhook](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/webhooks/update-webhook)
- [Delete webhook](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/webhooks/delete-webhook)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://api.resend.com` |
| `base_url_env` | `RESEND_API_URL` |
| Credential | `RESEND_API_KEY` (bearer) |

Assumptions:

- **RS1** (verified, [source](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/api-keys/create-api-key)): `POST /api-keys` creates an API key from `name` (at most 50 characters), `permission` (`full_access` or `sending_access`) and `domain_id` (with `sending_access` only), answering `{ id, token }`; requests carry `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.
- **RS2** (verified, [source](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/api-keys/list-api-keys)): `GET /api-keys` answers `{ object: list, has_more, data: [{ id, name, created_at, last_used_at }] }`, every key when no `limit` is sent, and never the token: the token is shown only in the create answer, so it is a once-only output.
- **RS3** (verified, [source](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/api-keys/delete-api-key)): `DELETE /api-keys/{api_key_id}` removes a key; there is no endpoint to read or change one key, so its permission and domain are sent on create and never compared.
- **RS4** (verified, [source](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/webhooks/create-webhook)): `POST /webhooks` creates a webhook from `endpoint` and `events` (both required), answering `{ object, id, signing_secret }`.
- **RS5** (verified, [source](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/webhooks/get-webhook)): `GET /webhooks/{webhook_id}` answers the webhook with `status` (`enabled`/`disabled`), `endpoint`, `events` and `signing_secret`: the secret stays readable, so it is an ordinary sensitive output.
- **RS6** (verified, [source](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/webhooks/list-webhooks)): `GET /webhooks` answers `{ object: list, has_more, data: [{ id, created_at, status, endpoint, events }] }`, every webhook when no `limit` is sent.
- **RS7** (verified, [source](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/webhooks/update-webhook)): `PATCH /webhooks/{webhook_id}` changes `endpoint`, `events` and `status`; `DELETE` on the same path removes the webhook.
- **RS8** **(unverified)**: Key names and webhook endpoints are not unique in Resend: the recipe takes the name (keys) and the endpoint URL (webhooks) as the identity, and refuses (PARAM_INVALID) when two match, so give each environment its own name and URL.
- **RS9** **(unverified)**: Creating a key or a webhook needs a `full_access` key; a deleted object answers 404.

### `resend.api_key`

**API key** (`http.resource`). A restricted API key per environment, such as `sponson-preview-pr-42` allowed only to send from one domain. Its token is a once-only output: pass it to the app's environment line in the same run (`{ from: <line>.token }`); later runs keep what that line holds, and `apply --recreate <line>` issues a new one. Only its existence is compared for drift: Resend shows no permission or domain for a key.

Covers: `resend-key-webhook` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`, `token` (sensitive, [once](plan-format.md#once-only-outputs): only from the create). On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | The key's name, unique among the account's keys (RS8); its identity. Matches `^.{1,50}$`. |
| `permission` | string | no | `sending_access` | What the key may do. One of `full_access`, `sending_access`. |
| `domain_id` | string | no | — | With `sending_access`, the only domain the key may send from. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: api_key
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: resend.api_key
  name: sponson-${ctx.env}-${ctx.scope}
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
find:
  path: /api-keys
  list_path: /data
  match:
    name: { param: name }
create:
  path: /api-keys
  body:
    permission: { param: permission }
    domain_id: { param: domain_id }
delete:
  path: /api-keys/{id}
outputs:
  token:
    path: /token
    sensitive: true
    once: true
```

### `resend.webhook`

**Webhook** (`http.resource`). A webhook delivering an environment's email events to its URL, such as the preview's `/api/resend` handler. Located by its endpoint URL; a console edit of its events is drift (its enabled/disabled status is left to the console: the create request takes none). Its signing secret is a sensitive output, readable on every run.

Covers: `resend-key-webhook` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`, `signing_secret` (sensitive). On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `endpoint` | string | yes | — | The URL events are delivered to; its identity (RS8). Matches `^https://\\S+$`. |
| `events` | list | yes | — | The event types to deliver, such as `email.delivered` and `email.bounced`. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: webhook
  adapter: http
```

## SendGrid

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/sendgrid.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/sendgrid.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Create an Event Webhook](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/webhooks/create-an-event-webhook)
- [Get all Event Webhooks](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/webhooks/get-all-event-webhooks)
- [Get an Event Webhook](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/webhooks/get-an-event-webhook)
- [Update an Event Webhook](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/webhooks/update-an-event-webhook)
- [Delete an Event Webhook](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/webhooks/delete-an-event-webhook)
- [Create a parse setting](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/settings-inbound-parse/create-a-parse-setting)
- [Retrieve a specific parse setting](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/settings-inbound-parse/retrieve-a-specific-parse-setting)
- [Update a parse setting](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/settings-inbound-parse/update-a-parse-setting)
- [Delete a parse setting](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/settings-inbound-parse/delete-a-parse-setting)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://api.sendgrid.com` |
| `base_url_env` | `SENDGRID_API_URL` |
| Credential | `SENDGRID_API_KEY` (bearer) |

Assumptions:

- **SG1** (verified, [source](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/webhooks/create-an-event-webhook)): `POST /v3/user/webhooks/event/settings` creates an Event Webhook from `url` (required), `enabled`, one boolean per event type (`processed`, `delivered`, `dropped`, `deferred`, `bounce`, `open`, `click`, `spam_report`, `unsubscribe`, `group_unsubscribe`, `group_resubscribe`) and `friendly_name`, answering 201 with the webhook and its string `id`; requests carry the API key as `Authorization: Bearer`. EU regional subusers use `https://api.eu.sendgrid.com`.
- **SG2** (verified, [source](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/webhooks/create-an-event-webhook)): Each URL can be used by only one Event Webhook (a second create answers 400 naming the existing id), so the URL identifies the webhook; the number of webhooks is limited by the plan (400 beyond it).
- **SG3** (verified, [source](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/webhooks/get-all-event-webhooks)): `GET /v3/user/webhooks/event/settings/all` answers `{ max_allowed, webhooks: [...] }` with every webhook's settings and `id`.
- **SG4** (verified, [source](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/webhooks/update-an-event-webhook)): `PATCH /v3/user/webhooks/event/settings/{id}` requires `url` and updates the fields sent; `DELETE` on the same path answers 204, and 404 for an unknown id. Without an id these paths act on the oldest webhook, which the recipe never does (its paths always carry the id).
- **SG5** (verified, [source](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/webhooks/create-an-event-webhook)): Signature verification and its public key are set through a separate endpoint and are not part of the webhook's create or update; this recipe does not manage them.
- **SG6** (verified, [source](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/settings-inbound-parse/create-a-parse-setting)): `POST /v3/user/webhooks/parse/settings` creates an Inbound Parse setting from `url`, `hostname`, `spam_check` and `send_raw`, answering 201 with those four fields bare; `GET`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` (204) `/v3/user/webhooks/parse/settings/{hostname}` read, update and remove it. The hostname must be on a domain authenticated in SendGrid, with an MX record pointing at SendGrid.
- **SG7** **(unverified)**: A PATCH that leaves out an event flag keeps its current value (the documentation's examples send only `url`); the recipe sends every flag it compares anyway.
- **SG8** **(unverified)**: A parse setting for a hostname that exists already is refused with an error status (not documented which); the next run then finds it by its hostname.

### `sendgrid.event_webhook`

**Event Webhook** (`http.resource`). An Event Webhook delivering an environment's email events to its URL, such as the preview's `/api/sendgrid/events` handler. Located by its URL (unique in SendGrid); a console edit of its enabled flag, an event flag or its friendly name is drift.

Covers: `sendgrid-webhook` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | string | yes | — | The URL events are posted to; its identity (SG2). Matches `^https?://\\S+$`. |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | `true` | Whether events are posted. |
| `friendly_name` | string | no | — | A label for the webhook (not unique). |
| `processed` | boolean | no | `false` | Post `processed` events. |
| `delivered` | boolean | no | `true` | Post `delivered` events. |
| `dropped` | boolean | no | `true` | Post `dropped` events. |
| `deferred` | boolean | no | `false` | Post `deferred` events. |
| `bounce` | boolean | no | `true` | Post `bounce` events. |
| `open` | boolean | no | `false` | Post `open` events. |
| `click` | boolean | no | `false` | Post `click` events. |
| `spam_report` | boolean | no | `true` | Post `spam_report` events. |
| `unsubscribe` | boolean | no | `false` | Post `unsubscribe` events. |
| `group_unsubscribe` | boolean | no | `false` | Post `group_unsubscribe` events. |
| `group_resubscribe` | boolean | no | `false` | Post `group_resubscribe` events. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: event_webhook
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: sendgrid.event_webhook
  url: https://${ctx.scope}.preview.example.com/api/sendgrid/events
  friendly_name: sponson ${ctx.env} ${ctx.scope}
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
find:
  path: /v3/user/webhooks/event/settings/all
  list_path: /webhooks
  match:
    url: { param: url }
create:
  path: /v3/user/webhooks/event/settings
update:
  method: PATCH
  path: /v3/user/webhooks/event/settings/{id}
  body:
    url: { param: url }
delete:
  path: /v3/user/webhooks/event/settings/{id}
fields:
  enabled: { param: enabled }
  friendly_name: { param: friendly_name }
  processed: { param: processed }
  delivered: { param: delivered }
  dropped: { param: dropped }
  deferred: { param: deferred }
  bounce: { param: bounce }
  open: { param: open }
  click: { param: click }
```

### `sendgrid.parse_setting`

**Inbound Parse setting** (`http.resource`). An Inbound Parse host per environment, such as `pr-42.parse.example.com`, posting the mail it receives to the environment's URL. Named by its hostname; a console edit of its URL, spam check or raw flag is drift. The hostname's domain must be authenticated in SendGrid and its MX record point at SendGrid (a wildcard record serves every environment).

Covers: `sendgrid-webhook` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| `url` | string | yes | — | The URL parsed mail is posted to. Matches `^https?://\\S+$`. |
| `spam_check` | boolean | no | `false` | Check mail for spam before posting it. |
| `send_raw` | boolean | no | `false` | Post the original MIME message. |
